response: No, the Barthel Index alone is not an adequate measure of outcome for longer-term quality of life in stroke patients. While it is a widely used and well-established measure of activities of daily living (ADLs), it has limitations in capturing the full range of outcomes, such as cognitive function, emotional well-being, social participation, and overall health-related quality of life. A more comprehensive assessment, including other standardized measures and patient-reported outcomes, is necessary to fully evaluate the longer-term quality of life and outcome in stroke patients.
